stem.text: The height of a weather balloon is H(t) meters, t seconds after it is released. Suppose that \( \left. \frac{dH}{dt} \right|_{t=2} = 1 \). Write this statement in prime notation, and state what it means.

answer_key.label: \( H'(2) = 1 \), so the rate of change of the height of the balloon with respect to time when t = 2 is 1 meters per second.

worked_solution.text: In \( \left. \frac{dH}{dt} \right|_{t=2} \) the function is H, the independent variable is t, and the derivative is evaluated at t = 2, so the statement is about one input only.
In prime notation the same statement is \( H'(2) = 1 \).
It says that the rate of change of the height of the balloon with respect to time when t = 2 is 1 meters per second.

options.label: \( \frac{H(2)}{2} = 1 \), so the height of the balloon divided by time when t = 2 is 1 meters per second.
options.derivation: the Leibniz fraction read as the quotient of the two quantities at the point

options.label: \( H'(2) = 1 \), so the rate of change of the height of the balloon with respect to time when t = 2 is 1 meters per second.
\( H'(t) = 1 \), so the rate of change of the height of the balloon with respect to time, the same at every t, is 1 meters per second.
options.derivation: the point of evaluation dropped, so a value at one input is read as the derivative function

options.label: \( H'(2) = 1 \), so the rate of change of time with respect to the height of the balloon when t = 2 is 1 seconds per meter.
options.derivation: the roles of the two variables exchanged, so the derivative is read with respect to the dependent variable
